A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Nf2/MERLIN acts as a tumor suppressor gene for liver stem/progenitors by controlling the abundance of EGFR and the EGFR signaling pathway.
Nf2 is required to maintain a quiescent progenitor cell pool in the liver.

loss of the tumor suppressor Nf2 in the liver causes a dramatic and progressive expansion of liver progenitor/stem cells, leading to the development of both cholangiocarcinoma and hepatocellular carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nf 2 gene, which is mutated in a variety of human cancers and neurofibromatous disorders, is required for maintaining a healthy balance in the liver between progenitor cells and hepatocytes.
Nf2 is a tumor suppressor gene that controls the maintenance and activation (proliferation) of the liver stem/progenitors cells (LSPCs).
